questions.stem: Multiplying a mass in kilograms by a velocity in metres per second gives momentum measured in:

options.explanation: Newtons measure force, not momentum.
The momentum unit is the mass unit times the velocity unit.
That squared unit belongs to acceleration.
That divides the units instead of multiplying them.

questions.stem: A parked car has no momentum at all because its:

options.explanation: The equation never mentions engines.
The car's mass is unchanged; mass alone never sets momentum.

options.text: velocity is zero, and p = m × v then gives zero
options.explanation: Anything multiplied by a zero velocity comes out at zero.

options.text: parked objects are exempt from the momentum law
options.explanation: The law covers every object; parked ones simply score zero.

questions.stem: Which of these does not change an object's momentum?

options.text: Keeping the mass and velocity exactly as they were
options.explanation: With both factors fixed, the product m × v is fixed too.
A changed velocity changes the product m × v.

options.text: Reversing the object's direction of travel
options.explanation: Direction is part of velocity, so the momentum changes.

options.text: Loading extra mass onto the object
options.explanation: A changed mass changes the product m × v.

questions.stem: A 60 g tennis ball rolls at 2 m/s towards a wall and bounces straight back at the same speed. Taking the approach direction as positive, its momentum after the bounce is:

options.explanation: That is the approach momentum; the return trip flips the sign.
The ball still moves after the bounce, so its momentum is not zero.
Nothing doubles: the speed is unchanged, only the direction reverses.
The size is 0.060 kg × 2 m/s = 0.12 kg m/s, and the reversed direction makes it negative.

questions.stem: Two identical trolleys roll along the same line at the same speed, one heading right and one heading left. Their momenta are:

options.text: equal in size and in sign
options.explanation: Ignoring direction hides the sign difference.

options.text: both zero, because the speeds match
options.explanation: Matching speeds do not cancel anything.

options.text: equal in size but opposite in sign
options.explanation: Same mass and speed give the same size; opposite travel gives opposite signs.
The equation compares momenta along one line without trouble.

questions.stem: Write down the momentum equation and give the unit of each quantity in it.
questions.modelAnswer: p = m × v, with momentum p in kilogram metres per second (kg m/s), mass m in kilograms and velocity v in metres per second.

questions.stem: State two changes that will alter an object's momentum.
questions.modelAnswer: Any change of velocity — speeding up, slowing down or turning — will do it, and so will a change of mass.

questions.stem: Explain why momentum is positive for one traveller and negative for another moving the opposite way along the same line.
questions.modelAnswer: Momentum takes its direction from velocity, and velocity is a vector. Once one side of the line is chosen as positive, a traveller heading the other way scores a negative momentum of the same size.

questions.stem: A trolley of mass 0.5 kg rolls at 4 m/s. Calculate its momentum, then give the momentum of an identical trolley moving at 4 m/s in the opposite direction.
questions.modelAnswer: p = m × v = 0.5 × 4 = 2 kg m/s. The second trolley has the same size momentum but the opposite sign, so −2 kg m/s.

questions.stem: During a collision between two trolleys with no external forces acting, the total momentum of the system:

options.explanation: Speed lost by one object is gained by another; the total holds.
Nothing adds momentum when no external force acts.
The rule covers collisions and explosions alike.

options.text: is the same before and after the collision
options.explanation: That equality is exactly what conservation states.

questions.stem: Conservation of momentum applies to which interactions?

options.explanation: The principle is stated for both kinds of interaction.
Explosions are covered too.
Collisions are covered too.
No such mass condition appears in the principle.

questions.stem: A 1 kg trolley rolls right at 3 m/s towards a 2 kg trolley at rest. Taking right as positive, the total momentum of the pair before they meet is:

options.explanation: That multiplies the combined mass by the speed.
That multiplies the resting trolley's mass by the speed, but a resting object contributes zero.
Only the moving trolley counts: 1 × 3 = 3 kg m/s.
The moving trolley does carry momentum, so the total is not zero.

questions.stem: Two trolleys collide; one rebounds afterwards and travels back the way it came. In the conservation equation, that trolley's momentum after the collision is:

options.explanation: Reversal changes the sign, not the size, of the momentum.

options.text: negative, because its velocity now points the other way
options.explanation: A reversed velocity enters the total with a minus sign.

options.text: positive, because momentum cannot be negative
options.explanation: Momentum is a vector, so it can be negative.

options.text: left out entirely once it rebounds
options.explanation: Rebounding objects stay in the system and in the equation.

questions.stem: Two skaters glide towards each other along one line at equal speeds. The overall momentum of the pair is:

options.explanation: Sizes add only when the directions agree.
The opposite signs remove half of the sum.
Opposite motions are handled by the sign convention.

options.text: zero, because the equal and opposite momenta cancel
options.explanation: Equal sizes with opposite signs sum to zero.

questions.stem: State the principle of conservation of momentum.
questions.modelAnswer: With no external forces acting, the total momentum before an interaction equals the total momentum after it.

questions.stem: Name the two kinds of interaction the conservation rule covers.
questions.modelAnswer: Collisions, where objects run into each other, and explosions, where a body splits into parts that fly apart.

questions.stem: Explain why two objects moving in opposite directions at the same speed can have zero total momentum.
questions.modelAnswer: Momentum is a vector, so the two objects carry equal-sized momenta with opposite signs. The signs cancel in the sum, leaving a total of zero even though both objects are still moving.

questions.stem: A toy car of mass 0.035 kg rolls at 0.8 m/s into a stationary toy van of mass 0.085 kg. Afterwards the car keeps moving at 0.1 m/s. Calculate the van's velocity, assuming momentum is conserved.
questions.modelAnswer: Before: the car has 0.035 × 0.8 = 0.028 kg m/s and the van adds nothing, so the total is 0.028 kg m/s. After: the car holds 0.035 × 0.1 = 0.0035 kg m/s, so the van's momentum is 0.028 − 0.0035 = 0.0245 kg m/s. Dividing by its 0.085 kg mass gives v = 0.0245 ÷ 0.085 ≈ 0.29 m/s in the car's original direction.
